programme.displayName: RDS, EC2, and Application Load Balancer Follow Along
programme.subtitle: Create a private RDS for MySQL database, authorize EC2 through security groups, and prove the ALB-to-EC2 web path.
programme.description: In eu-west-2, use an existing VPC with subnets in at least two Availability Zones. Create separate security groups for an internet-facing Application Load Balancer (ALB), an EC2 web server, and a private Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance. The ALB forwards HTTP requests to EC2. The RDS security group permits MySQL traffic only from the EC2 security group.
programme.learningOutcome: Create an RDS DB instance and a security-group chain where the path is client → ALB → EC2, while EC2 is authorized to reach RDS on MySQL port 3306. Verify a healthy ALB target, the static web response, the available DB instance, and the EC2-to-RDS security-group rule.

tasks.title: Create the three security groups and their inbound rules
tasks.goal: Create an ALB security group, an EC2 security group, and an RDS security group with a least-privilege inbound path.
tasks.whyItMatters: The ALB needs HTTP from clients, the EC2 web server needs HTTP only from the ALB, and RDS for MySQL needs port 3306 only from EC2.

consoleSteps.title: Create the ALB group
consoleSteps.instruction: ☐ Create security group fa-rds-alb-ec2-alb-sg in [VPC_ID].

instructions.text: ☐ Create security group fa-rds-alb-ec2-alb-sg in [VPC_ID].

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The ALB security group exists.
consoleSteps.warning: Create the group only in [VPC_ID].

consoleSteps.title: Allow client HTTP
consoleSteps.instruction: ☐ Add inbound HTTP port 80 from 0.0.0.0/0 to fa-rds-alb-ec2-alb-sg.

instructions.text: ☐ Add inbound HTTP port 80 from 0.0.0.0/0 to fa-rds-alb-ec2-alb-sg.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The ALB group permits public HTTP requests.
consoleSteps.warning: This is intentionally public for a short-lived HTTP test.

consoleSteps.title: Create the EC2 group
consoleSteps.instruction: ☐ Create security group fa-rds-alb-ec2-web-sg in [VPC_ID].

instructions.text: ☐ Create security group fa-rds-alb-ec2-web-sg in [VPC_ID].

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The EC2 security group exists.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not add SSH access for this Follow Along.

consoleSteps.title: Allow ALB-to-EC2 HTTP
consoleSteps.instruction: ☐ Add inbound HTTP port 80 from fa-rds-alb-ec2-alb-sg to fa-rds-alb-ec2-web-sg.

instructions.text: ☐ Add inbound HTTP port 80 from fa-rds-alb-ec2-alb-sg to fa-rds-alb-ec2-web-sg.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: Only instances using the ALB group can reach the EC2 web port.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not use a public CIDR source for this EC2 rule.

consoleSteps.title: Create the RDS group
consoleSteps.instruction: ☐ Create security group fa-rds-alb-ec2-rds-sg in [VPC_ID].

instructions.text: ☐ Create security group fa-rds-alb-ec2-rds-sg in [VPC_ID].

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The RDS security group exists.
consoleSteps.warning: Create the group only in [VPC_ID].

consoleSteps.title: Allow EC2-to-RDS MySQL
consoleSteps.instruction: ☐ Add inbound MySQL port 3306 from fa-rds-alb-ec2-web-sg to fa-rds-alb-ec2-rds-sg.

instructions.text: ☐ Add inbound MySQL port 3306 from fa-rds-alb-ec2-web-sg to fa-rds-alb-ec2-rds-sg.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: Only instances using the EC2 web security group are authorized to initiate MySQL traffic to RDS.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not permit port 3306 from 0.0.0.0/0.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-security-group --group-name fa-rds-alb-ec2-alb-sg --description "ALB HTTP for RDS EC2 Follow Along" --vpc-id [VPC_ID] --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Replace [VPC_ID] with the VPC recorded in Task 1 and record the returned GroupId as [ALB_SG_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response includes a GroupId.
cliSteps.warning: Security-group names must be unique within the VPC.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id [ALB_SG_ID] --protocol tcp --port 80 --cidr 0.0.0.0/0 --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Replace [ALB_SG_ID] with the ID returned by the preceding command.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response returns true and includes an inbound TCP port 80 rule.
cliSteps.warning: This allows public HTTP access to the ALB only; it does not expose EC2 or RDS directly.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-security-group --group-name fa-rds-alb-ec2-web-sg --description "EC2 HTTP from ALB for RDS Follow Along" --vpc-id [VPC_ID] --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Replace [VPC_ID] with the VPC recorded in Task 1 and record the returned GroupId as [WEB_SG_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response includes a GroupId.
cliSteps.warning: Do not reuse the ALB security group for the EC2 instance.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id [WEB_SG_ID] --protocol tcp --port 80 --source-group [ALB_SG_ID] --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Replace [WEB_SG_ID] and [ALB_SG_ID] with IDs returned by the preceding security-group commands.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response returns true and references [ALB_SG_ID] as the inbound source.
cliSteps.warning: The source security group must be in the same VPC or a peer VPC.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-security-group --group-name fa-rds-alb-ec2-rds-sg --description "RDS MySQL from EC2 for Follow Along" --vpc-id [VPC_ID] --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Replace [VPC_ID] with the VPC recorded in Task 1 and record the returned GroupId as [RDS_SG_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response includes a GroupId.
cliSteps.warning: Do not attach this group to the ALB.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id [RDS_SG_ID] --protocol tcp --port 3306 --source-group [WEB_SG_ID] --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Replace [RDS_SG_ID] and [WEB_SG_ID] with the recorded group IDs.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response returns true and references [WEB_SG_ID] as the inbound source.
cliSteps.warning: Port 3306 is the default port for RDS for MySQL.

verification.title: Confirm the security-group path
verification.instruction: Inspect the three inbound rule sets and confirm: public HTTP → ALB group, ALB group → EC2 group, and EC2 group → RDS group on port 3306.
verification.expectedResult: No rule directly allows public traffic to the EC2 web group or RDS group.

consoleSteps.title: Set the DB identifier

instructions.text: ☐ Set the DB instance identifier to fa-rds-alb-ec2-db.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The identifier is recorded on the form.
consoleSteps.warning: Use this exact name only for this Follow Along.

consoleSteps.title: Use managed credentials
consoleSteps.instruction: ☐ Select the managed master-password option.

instructions.text: ☐ Select the managed master-password option.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: RDS manages the master password instead of displaying a sample password in this Follow Along.

consoleSteps.title: Set private connectivity

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The selected DB subnet group is displayed.

consoleSteps.title: Attach the RDS group
consoleSteps.instruction: ☐ Select fa-rds-alb-ec2-rds-sg as the VPC security group.

instructions.text: ☐ Select fa-rds-alb-ec2-rds-sg as the VPC security group.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The RDS security group is attached.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not add the ALB security group to the DB instance.

cliSteps.command: aws rds create-db-subnet-group --db-subnet-group-name fa-rds-alb-ec2-subnets --db-subnet-group-description "Two AZ subnets for RDS ALB EC2 Follow Along" --subnet-ids [SUBNET_A_ID] [SUBNET_B_ID] --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Replace the subnet placeholders with the two IDs recorded in Task 1.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response shows DBSubnetGroupName fa-rds-alb-ec2-subnets and status Complete.
cliSteps.warning: The subnets must be in at least two Availability Zones.

cliSteps.command: aws rds create-db-instance --db-instance-identifier fa-rds-alb-ec2-db --db-name appdb --allocated-storage 20 --db-instance-class db.t3.micro --engine mysql --master-username appadmin --manage-master-user-password --vpc-security-group-ids [RDS_SG_ID] --db-subnet-group-name fa-rds-alb-ec2-subnets --backup-retention-period 1 --no-publicly-accessible --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Replace [RDS_SG_ID] with the RDS group ID from Task 2. The command uses RDS-managed master-password management and intentionally includes no password.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains a DBInstances entry with DBInstanceIdentifier fa-rds-alb-ec2-db and an initial creating status.
cliSteps.warning: The DB instance and its retained backups can incur charges. Confirm the selected engine version and DB instance class are offered in eu-west-2 before running the command.

cliSteps.command: aws rds wait db-instance-available --db-instance-identifier fa-rds-alb-ec2-db --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Wait for the DB instance created by the prior command to reach the available state.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command returns after the DB instance becomes available.
cliSteps.warning: The waiter polls every 30 seconds and can end with a nonzero result if availability is not reached in time.

cliSteps.command: aws rds describe-db-instances --db-instance-identifier fa-rds-alb-ec2-db --query 'DBInstances[0].{Status:DBInstanceStatus,Endpoint:Endpoint.Address,Port:Endpoint.Port,Public:PubliclyAccessible}' --output table --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Record the endpoint as [RDS_ENDPOINT] for reference only; it is not a password.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The table shows Status available, port 3306, a DB endpoint, and Public false.
cliSteps.warning: Do not publish the DB endpoint or attempt to connect from the public internet.

verification.title: Confirm the private database state
verification.instruction: Confirm that fa-rds-alb-ec2-db is Available, Publicly accessible is false, and its attached security group is fa-rds-alb-ec2-rds-sg.
verification.expectedResult: The DB is available and is not configured for public access.

cliSteps.command: aws ssm get-parameter --name /aws/service/ami-amazon-linux-latest/al2023-ami-kernel-default-x86_64 --query 'Parameter.Value' --output text --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Record the returned AMI ID as [AL2023_AMI_ID]. This value is required by the following EC2 launch command.
cliSteps.expectedResult: An AMI ID is returned.
cliSteps.warning: Confirm that the returned AMI is appropriate for your account architecture before launching it.

cliSteps.command:
aws ec2 run-instances --image-id [AL2023_AMI_ID] --instance-type t3.micro --count 1 --subnet-id [SUBNET_A_ID] --security-group-ids [WEB_SG_ID] --user-data '#!/bin/bash dnf install -y httpd echo "

RDS network authorization is verified separately.

" > /var/www/html/index.html systemctl enable --now httpd' --tag-specifications 'ResourceType=instance,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-rds-alb-ec2-web}]' --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Replace [AL2023_AMI_ID] with the AMI ID returned by the prior command, [SUBNET_A_ID] with one subnet from Task 1, and [WEB_SG_ID] with the EC2 security-group ID from Task 2. Record the returned instance ID as [EC2_INSTANCE_ID].

cliSteps.expectedResult: The instance state progresses to running and the output shows its private IP, subnet, and security-group ID.

cliSteps.command: aws elbv2 create-target-group --name fa-rds-alb-ec2-tg --protocol HTTP --port 80 --target-type instance --vpc-id [VPC_ID] --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Replace [VPC_ID] with the VPC ID from Task 1 and record the returned TargetGroupArn as [TARGET_GROUP_ARN].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response includes a target group with HTTP protocol, port 80, and instance target type.
cliSteps.warning: The target group must be in the same VPC as the EC2 target.

cliSteps.command: aws elbv2 register-targets --target-group-arn [TARGET_GROUP_ARN] --targets Id=[EC2_INSTANCE_ID],Port=80 --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Replace [TARGET_GROUP_ARN] and [EC2_INSTANCE_ID] with values returned by previous commands.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command registers the instance with the target group.
cliSteps.warning: The EC2 security group must allow the ALB security group on the listener and health-check port.

cliSteps.command: aws elbv2 create-load-balancer --name fa-rds-alb-ec2 --type application --scheme internet-facing --ip-address-type ipv4 --subnets [SUBNET_A_ID] [SUBNET_B_ID] --security-groups [ALB_SG_ID] --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Replace the subnet and security-group placeholders with values recorded in Tasks 1 and 2. Record the returned LoadBalancerArn as [ALB_ARN].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response includes an application load balancer with an ARN and DNS name.
cliSteps.warning: Application Load Balancers require subnets from at least two Availability Zones.

cliSteps.command: aws elbv2 create-listener --load-balancer-arn [ALB_ARN] --protocol HTTP --port 80 --default-actions Type=forward,TargetGroupArn=[TARGET_GROUP_ARN] --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Replace [ALB_ARN] and [TARGET_GROUP_ARN] with values returned by the preceding ALB and target-group commands.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response includes an HTTP listener that forwards to the target group.
cliSteps.warning: This intentionally uses unencrypted HTTP only for this temporary beginner test.

verification.title: Confirm the routing configuration
verification.instruction: Confirm that fa-rds-alb-ec2 has an HTTP listener on port 80 whose default action forwards to fa-rds-alb-ec2-tg.
verification.expectedResult: The ALB listener is associated with the target group.

tasks.title: Verify the ALB response and the authorized RDS network path
tasks.feature: RDS, EC2, and Application Load Balancer verification
tasks.goal: Prove the ALB reaches a healthy EC2 target and verify that the RDS instance is available with the EC2 security group authorized on port 3306.
tasks.whyItMatters: A healthy target and browser response prove ALB-to-EC2 routing. The RDS status and referenced security-group rule prove the intended EC2-to-RDS network authorization.

consoleSteps.title: Check target health
consoleSteps.instruction: ☐ Open the Targets tab for fa-rds-alb-ec2-tg.

instructions.text: ☐ Open the Targets tab for fa-rds-alb-ec2-tg.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The registered EC2 target is listed.
consoleSteps.warning: Initial health checks can take several minutes after user data finishes.

consoleSteps.title: Confirm target health
consoleSteps.instruction: ☐ Wait for the EC2 target state to become healthy.

instructions.text: ☐ Wait for the EC2 target state to become healthy.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The target state is healthy.
consoleSteps.warning: If the target is unhealthy, check the EC2 web security group and user-data completion.

consoleSteps.title: Open the ALB DNS name
consoleSteps.instruction: ☐ Open the ALB DNS name in a browser.

instructions.text: ☐ Open the ALB DNS name in a browser.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The page says ALB to EC2 test succeeded.
consoleSteps.warning: This proves the ALB-to-EC2 HTTP path only; it does not run a database query.

consoleSteps.title: Check DB status
consoleSteps.instruction: ☐ Open fa-rds-alb-ec2-db in the RDS console.

instructions.text: ☐ Open fa-rds-alb-ec2-db in the RDS console.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The DB instance status is Available.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not expose or copy a database password.

consoleSteps.title: Check DB access rule
consoleSteps.instruction: ☐ Inspect the inbound rule on fa-rds-alb-ec2-rds-sg.

instructions.text: ☐ Inspect the inbound rule on fa-rds-alb-ec2-rds-sg.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: TCP 3306 lists fa-rds-alb-ec2-web-sg as its source.
consoleSteps.warning: This is network authorization, not a successful database login test.

cliSteps.command: aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn [TARGET_GROUP_ARN] --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Replace [TARGET_GROUP_ARN] with the target-group ARN from Task 5.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response reports the EC2 target with TargetHealth state healthy after initial checks complete.
cliSteps.warning: An initial or unhealthy result means the target is not yet ready for ALB routing.

cliSteps.command: aws elbv2 describe-load-balancers --names fa-rds-alb-ec2 --query 'LoadBalancers[0].DNSName' --output text --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Record the returned DNS name and open it in a browser to view the static page.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command returns the ALB DNS name.
cliSteps.warning: Use the DNS name only for this temporary HTTP verification.

cliSteps.command: aws rds describe-db-instances --db-instance-identifier fa-rds-alb-ec2-db --query 'DBInstances[0].{Status:DBInstanceStatus,Public:PubliclyAccessible,Port:Endpoint.Port,SecurityGroups:VpcSecurityGroups[*].VpcSecurityGroupId}' --output table --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Verify that the database is available, not public, uses port 3306, and lists [RDS_SG_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The table shows Status available, Public false, Port 3306, and the RDS security-group ID.
cliSteps.warning: This command does not test database authentication.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 describe-security-groups --group-ids [RDS_SG_ID] --query 'SecurityGroups[0].IpPermissions' --output json --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Replace [RDS_SG_ID] with the RDS security-group ID from Task 2 and confirm that the TCP 3306 rule references [WEB_SG_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The output includes an inbound rule for TCP port 3306 with the EC2 web security group as its source.
cliSteps.warning: A security-group rule authorizes a network path but does not replace database authentication.

verification.title: Record the proof
verification.instruction: Record the healthy target state, the browser page text, the DB available state, and the RDS inbound rule that references the EC2 web security group.
verification.expectedResult: You have evidence of ALB → EC2 routing and EC2 → RDS network authorization.

findings.message: The requested architecture is correctly interpreted as client → ALB → EC2, with EC2 authorized to reach RDS. An Application Load Balancer routes HTTP/HTTPS requests to registered targets such as EC2 instances; it does not directly connect to an RDS DB instance.

The static browser page intentionally proves only ALB-to-EC2 routing. A genuine application-level RDS query would require a secure runtime method for the EC2 application to obtain database authentication material. This Follow Along intentionally does not provide credentials, an IAM policy, or a secret-retrieval design.
Before running the RDS create command, manually confirm that the selected MySQL engine version and db.t3.micro DB instance class are available for your account in eu-west-2.

Before launching EC2, manually confirm that the selected subnet supports the required first-boot package installation and that the AMI ID returned by the public Amazon Linux parameter suits your required CPU architecture.

When deleting the RDS DB instance, manually review whether the RDS-managed secret remains in your account and whether you need a final DB snapshot. Retain or delete only items associated with fa-rds-alb-ec2-db according to your data-retention decision.
